regime.label: Energy shock + memory shock; a calm index hiding violent single-stock dispersion
regime.note: SPY closed 746.82 (+0.69%) on 7/31 — a quiet index masking AAPL -7.3%, AMD -6.7% from its own open, and a six-name energy sleeve up 1.2-2.4%. Two independent physical supply shocks now drive the tape: crude (US-Iran, Hormuz) and DRAM/HBM (hyperscaler pull). Both are supply-side, both are dated, and the market is pricing them name by name rather than at the index level.

analyst.thesis:
What changed since last tick is that I can finally name my own error. For three ticks I described energy as a 'fading hedge' and cut it to a 2%+2% token, while energy was in fact the strongest sleeve in the entire universe: over the last 20 sessions ERX +24.0%, FANG +18.0%, OXY +16.7%, CVX +16.3%, COP +15.1%, XOM +13.4%, against SPY +0.3%. Brent sits near $86 yet is up more than 20% for the month of July. I had the price level roughly right and my positioning exactly backwards.

The forward trade is not to chase that. It is to rotate from the energy names whose catalyst is now SPENT into the ones whose catalyst is still ahead. XOM and CVX both reported this morning: CVX beat and closed +2.4%, XOM missed and closed -1.0% — and XOM's miss was specifically downstream, scheduled refinery maintenance eating a windfall that upstream realizations had already earned. That is a company-specific, segment-specific drag. The three pure upstream E&Ps in this universe carry no refining segment at all, and all three report inside the next four sessions: FANG 8/3 pm, DVN 8/4 pm, COP 8/6 am. They book the same Q2 price deck that produced the integrateds' windfall, without the refining offset that produced the miss.

Consensus appears to be reading XOM's headline miss as an energy-sector datapoint — yet every energy name in the universe rose on 7/31 anyway, which tells me the tape is already separating the two stories and I am early rather than alone. What I expect differently: upstream-only Q2 prints that beat on realizations, guided into a Q3 whose price deck is 20% higher than the quarter being reported. DVN is the anchor because it is the cheapest way to own that at 12.3x trailing earnings against COP's 20.1x, XOM's 26.5x and CVX's 33.3x.

The second half of the thesis is a refusal. AMD reports 8/4 and I am cutting it to zero before that print. The memory shortage stopped being a narrative today: Apple's own guidance put component shortages into forward numbers, DRAM spot is up roughly 700% year over year, and Intel has said publicly there is no relief until 2028. AMD's MI-series accelerators are HBM-hungry, so scarce memory is both a cost line and a units ceiling for exactly the quarter it is about to guide — and it trades at 141x trailing earnings. I do not want to own that combination into a dated print I cannot handicap favorably.

evidence.point: Energy is the strongest 20-session sleeve in the universe: FANG +18.0%, OXY +16.7%, CVX +16.3%, COP +15.1%, XOM +13.4%, DVN +11.5% vs SPY +0.3% over the same 20 sessions.

evidence.point: Brent 'fell to around $86 per barrel on Friday, but was still on track to gain more than 20% for the month as of July 31st'; Cushing storage 'drawn down significantly'; direct strikes on energy infrastructure 'could push Brent beyond $95 per barrel'.

XOM's miss was downstream, not price-deck: 'scheduled maintenance costs ate into Exxon's bottom line, leading earnings to miss expectations' and 'limited refinery capacity prevented the oil giant from higher windfalls in oil profits last quarter.' CVX, on the same price deck, beat.
Every energy name rose on 7/31 despite XOM's headline miss — CVX +2.4%, DVN +2.2%, OXY +2.0%, FANG +1.6%, COP +1.2%, with XOM itself only -1.0%.
Valuation spread across the energy complex (trailing P/E): DVN 12.34, COP 20.07, XOM 26.45, CVX 33.29, OXY 63.95, FANG 224.52. DVN P/B 1.79, FANG P/B 1.54.
Verified forward catalysts inside four sessions: FANG 2026-08-03 pm, DVN 2026-08-04 pm, COP 2026-08-06 am, VRTX 2026-08-03 pm, LLY 2026-08-05 am (est EPS 8.84), AMD 2026-08-04 pm (est EPS 1.55).

Memory shock is now in forward guidance, not commentary: DRAM spot prices 'surged nearly 700% over the past year'; IDC sees 2026 smartphone shipments -12.9% and PC -11.3%; Micron has 'no line-of-sight as to when memory supply will be able to catch up'; Intel: 'There's no relief until 2028.'

AAPL FQ4 guide of 9-11% revenue growth vs >12% consensus, Services $30.7B vs ~$31.3B est, Greater China $18.8B vs $19.5B est; Cook flagged 'increasing impact' from the memory shortage. AAPL closed 309.03, -7.3%.
AMD traded 510.275 open / 515.62 high / 475.76 low / 476.24 close on 7/31 — a 6.7% collapse from its own open — at a trailing P/E of 140.98, three sessions before its 8/4 print.
PYPL trades at 11.03x trailing earnings, +25.8% over 20 sessions, 3.8% off its 52-week high, with the rejected $60.50 bid still framing downside.

risks: Concentration: DVN+COP+FANG+CVX is 42% of the book on ONE factor. A single Hormuz de-escalation headline breaks all four at once — this is deliberately not diversified, and it is the largest risk I am carrying.

Q2 prints report a June-quarter price deck; July's +20% shows up in guidance, not results. If the E&Ps guide conservatively on Q3 realizations, the catalyst resolves flat and I have paid up for three prints in four days.

FANG's 224.5x trailing P/E reflects depressed/impaired trailing earnings, not a growth multiple — if the impairment is structural rather than one-off, the P/B 1.54 support I am leaning on is weaker than it looks.

Cutting AMD before 8/4 is a directional refusal: if AMD beats and guides through the memory squeeze, I eat the whipsaw of filling at 490.18 on Friday's limit and selling near 476 on Monday's open, and I miss the rebound.

77% deployed is the most invested this book has been. The prior reflection blamed cash for the alpha gap and I have acted on it — but that also removes the buffer that has been cushioning a -12.9% all-time drawdown.
LLY reports 8/5 at a 43.6x P/E and 36.6x book; it is 8.1% off its 52-week high and has been a persistent drag. A second disappointing print turns a 14% anchor into the same mistake twice.

reflection.looking_back: Last tick I set targets LLY 16%, PYPL 12%, AMD 10%, VRTX 8%, BAC 4%, XOM 2%, CVX 2% — 54% deployed, up from 37% — with buy limits 1% over the close on AMD (490.18), LLY (1166.82) and VRTX (486.51), and resting trims on XOM and CVX. All three limits cross on the 7/31 session and fill. The book stands at -12.9% all-time against SPY -1.2%, alpha -11.7 points, annualized Sharpe -3.93 over 25 sessions. I said last tick I would stop building around macro narrative and start building around dated events; I did that, and the event-driven part worked while the macro read underneath it was still wrong.
worked: The limit discipline did precisely its job on two of three names: LLY's 7/31 open printed 1145.74 against my 1166.82 limit and VRTX's opened 480.16 against my 486.51, so both filled at the open — 1.8% and 1.3% better than my worst-case basis. Defaulting queued buys to a limit ~1% over the close is now proven, not theoretical.

Holding PYPL through an RSI-74.7 reading instead of mechanically trimming was right for a third straight tick: it closed 57.21 at 11.03x trailing earnings, +25.8% over 20 sessions and only 3.8% off its 52-week high, with the rejected $60.50 bid still framing the downside.
Raising deployment from 37% to 54% was directionally correct and I should have gone further — SPY rose only +0.69% on 7/31 while the sleeve I was underweight rose 1.2-2.4% across six names.
missed: The dominant error, and it is mine three ticks running: I called energy a 'fading hedge' and cut XOM and CVX to a 2%+2% token with resting trims on top — while energy was the strongest sleeve in the universe. Over 20 sessions ERX +24.0%, FANG +18.0%, OXY +16.7%, CVX +16.3%, COP +15.1%, XOM +13.4% against SPY +0.3%. I anchored on Brent falling from 96.78 to about 86 and never checked that it was still up more than 20% for the month. I had the level right and my positioning exactly inverted.

The AMD limit is the textbook failure my own playbook warned about in writing. I set a 1%-over-the-close buy limit at 490.18 on a name that opened 7/31 at 510.275 and collapsed to a 475.76 low, closing 476.24. The limit filled me at 490.18 on the way down and I am instantly -2.8%. A buy limit protects against a gap-UP and does nothing about a gap-down — the only defense against buying a falling knife is not entering, and I entered a 141x semiconductor three sessions before its print.

I named the memory shortage as the central mechanism two ticks in a row and still owned no position expressing it in either direction — not the suppliers, not a hedge, nothing. Identifying the driver of the tape and then not trading it is the most expensive kind of correct.

Sizing XOM and CVX at 2% each meant that even being right about energy would have been worth almost nothing to the book. Conviction that small is indistinguishable from no conviction, and it is a habit across the last three ticks.
reflection.adjustment: Rotate energy from spent catalysts into forward ones and size it like I mean it. XOM and CVX reported this morning, so their events are behind them: XOM goes to zero (its miss was refining, a drag the pure E&Ps do not carry) and CVX is capped at 5% as a yield-paying hold. The freed capital plus cash goes into the three pure upstream names that report inside four sessions — DVN 15% (8/4, 12.3x), COP 12% (8/6, 20.1x), FANG 10% (8/3, P/B 1.54) — for a 42% sleeve that is a real bet rather than a token. And I cut AMD to zero BEFORE its 8/4 print rather than holding 141x trailing earnings into a memory-cost squeeze I can name and date. Deployment goes 54% to 77%; cash has been the single largest contributor to an 11.7-point alpha gap and I am done paying for it.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 150 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Backtest reference
sources.detail: A separate Dec–Jun walk-forward backtest (2026-01-02–2026-07-31, in-sample, mostly-bull) is shown inside each rule strategy's detail for context only — it is NOT the live board.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Live account
sources.detail: Robinhood MCP, Agentic cash account ••••, via get_portfolio / get_equity_positions / get_equity_orders.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
